# 2 Chronicles Chapter 24 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother was Zibiah, from Beersheba.

**2** Joash did what was right in the LORD's eyes throughout the lifetime of Jehoiada the priest.

**3** Jehoiada chose two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.

**4** Some time later, Joash decided to restore the LORD's temple.

**5** He gathered the priests and Levites and said, "Go to the towns of Judah and collect money from all Israel for the annual repair of your God's temple. Do it right away." But the Levites dragged their feet.

**6** So the king called Jehoiada the chief priest and asked, "Why haven't you required the Levites to collect from Judah and Jerusalem the tax that Moses the LORD's servant imposed on the assembly of Israel for the tent of the covenant law?"

**7** (The followers of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into God's temple and used its sacred objects for Baal worship.)

**8** At the king's command, a chest was made and placed outside the gate of the LORD's temple.

**9** A proclamation was issued in Judah and Jerusalem requiring everyone to bring to the LORD the tax Moses the servant of God had imposed on Israel in the wilderness.

**10** All the officials and all the people gladly brought their contributions and dropped them into the chest until it was full.

**11** Whenever the Levites brought the chest to the king's officials and they saw it was overflowing with money, the royal secretary and the chief priest's officer would come, empty the chest, and carry it back to its place. They did this day after day and collected a large amount of money.

**12** The king and Jehoiada gave the money to those supervising the work on the LORD's temple. They hired stonemasons and carpenters to restore the temple, as well as iron and bronze workers to repair it.

**13** The workers were diligent, and the repairs progressed under their direction. They rebuilt God's temple according to its original design and reinforced it.

**14** When they finished, they brought the remaining money to the king and Jehoiada, and it was used to make articles for the LORD's temple — articles for worship and burnt offerings, dishes, and other objects of gold and silver. Burnt offerings were presented continually in the LORD's temple throughout Jehoiada's lifetime.

**15** Jehoiada grew old and full of years, and he died at the age of 130.

**16** He was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done so much good in Israel for God and His temple.

**17** After Jehoiada died, the officials of Judah came and paid homage to the king, and the king listened to them.

**18** They abandoned the temple of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and worshiped Asherah poles and idols. God's wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem because of their guilt.

**19** Although the LORD sent prophets to bring them back, they refused to listen, despite being warned.

**20** Then the Spirit of God came on Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood before the people and said, "This is what God says: 'Why do you disobey the LORD's commands? You will not prosper. Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you.'"

**21** But they plotted against him, and by order of the king, they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the LORD's temple.

**22** King Joash didn't remember the kindness that Zechariah's father Jehoiada had shown him. Instead, he killed Jehoiada's son. As Zechariah lay dying, he said, "May the LORD see this and call you to account."

**23** At the turn of the year, the Aramean army marched against Joash. They invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all the leaders of the people and sending all the plunder to their king in Damascus.

**24** Although the Aramean army came with only a small number of men, the LORD gave them victory over a much larger force, because Judah had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. So judgment was executed on Joash.

**25** When the Arameans withdrew, they left Joash badly wounded. His own officials conspired against him to avenge the murder of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they assassinated him in his bed. He was buried in the City of David, but not in the royal tombs.

**26** The conspirators were Zabad son of Shimeath, an Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith, a Moabite woman.

**27** The account of his sons, the many prophecies against him, and the rebuilding of God's temple are written in the annotations on the Book of the Kings. His son Amaziah succeeded him as king.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **24:2**: "Throughout the lifetime of Jehoiada" — five words that contain an entire tragedy. Joash is a borrowed-faith king. When the source of his faith dies, so does his faithfulness.

- **24:16**: A priest buried among kings. Let that sink in. Jehoiada earned what Joash was born into — and he earned it more.

- **24:22**: The king who was saved by a priest's family murders that priest's son. In the temple courtyard. Zechariah's dying words — "May the LORD see and call you to account" — are the last words the Chronicler wants you to hear before the judgment falls.

- **24:24**: A tiny Aramean force defeats a massive Judean army. The math is impossible — unless God is on the other side. This is the Chronicler's theology in reverse: abandon God, and your numbers don't matter.


— PNEUMA
